title.narrative: Multi-sectorial Integrated Response for conflict affected communities of West Gojjam Zone of Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgt ltspangtAccording to UNOCHA Situation Report, Last updated: 10 Jan 2024, Ethiopia is, once again, on the verge of a major humanitarian situation due to cycles of multiple, often overlapping crises, which severely weakens communities’ ability to cope. These crises are primarily driven by the convergence of four major factors: climate crises (flood and drought), armed conflicts, diseases, and economic shocks. The convergence of these shocks are pushing more people into displacement, food insecurity, malnutrition, disease outbreaks, and increased protection concerns amid rising global prices of essential commodities, inflation, and continual devaluation of the local currency.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtAs already mentioned above, the current situation in Amhara region is affecting the fragile education system, protection, WASH, and health sectors, with kids, girls, women, and older people who are most vulnerable. The region continues to face a heightened malnutrition caseload with recent data indicating the global acute malnutrition (GAM) rates at 21 percent for children and over 54 percent for pregnant and lactating women (PLW), exceeding the global threshold of 15 percent. Food insecurity situation is particularly concerning, especially since the current hostilities erupted during the harvest season and amid the food pause. The needs of about 591,857 internally displaced people (IDPs) in the region, including 90,322 IDPs in North Shewa Zone and Debre Birhan town, remain largely unmet. The current volatile situation in the region is posing additional challenges to the cholera response as well as delivery of supplies.ltbrgtThus, AEID plans to support the conflict-affected community of Marawi and Adet towns of West Gojjam Zone in Amhara Region. AEID will leverage its experience in humanitarian and development interventions in the areas. The proposed project will support the affected community in the WASH, Health and MPCA sectors. A total of 80,500 individuals are targeted in the two towns of North Mecha and Yilmana Dinsa woredas through:ltbrgtMPCA:ltbrgtestablishing beneficiary selection and registration committees and Compliant handling committeesltbrgtRegistration of beneficiaries for MPCAltbrgtProviding multi-purpose cash assistance for beneficiariesltbrgtConducting PDMltbrgtHealth:ltbrgtProviding 30 types of essential medical supplies for 12 health institutions which are not providing basic services for those who are in need due to medical supplies shortage,ltbrgtProviding basic health services through MHT.ltbrgtWASH:ltbrgtReplacement of electrical submersible pump for 22KW damaged by the conflict. ltbrgtReplacement of solar pumping component of 55KW pump damaged by the conflict. ltbrgt Replacement of solar pumping component of 22KW pump damaged by the conflict. ltbrgtEstablish effective, safe, and accessible community-based complaints mechanisms.ltbrgtlt/pgt
